text: Writing clean code is a skill that makes software easier to read and maintain. The most important rule is to make your code readable, as if you were writing for a human, not just a machine. To do this, follow clear naming conventions: use names that explain what a variable or function does, like `calculateTotal` instead of `ct` or `x`. Break your program into small, focused functions that each complete a single task. This approach not only simplifies testing but also improves maintainability, allowing you or other developers to update code quickly without breaking existing features. Clean code saves time, reduces errors, and, most importantly, respects your future self.
